findings.description: `reviewNode = snapshotNodes.find(candidate => candidate.kind === 'review' && !isChallengeNode(candidate))` is the only thing that stops captured-file findings from being read through the challenge node, which also has kind 'review' and comes first in a guarded graph. The guarded run is seeded with `review: null` (seed.ts:502, and no reviewResults entry), so findings-on-files, findings-by-reviewer and the file-findings panel never run on a graph that has a challenge node. challenge-node-page covers only the other exclusion (`isReview`, line 311, via `review-result` count 0).
findings.failure_scenario: Deleting `&& !isChallengeNode(candidate)` at line 316 passes all 31 browser tests. On a real guarded run whose review is recorded at attempt 1 and whose challenge has attempts 2, CreatedFiles would then fetch `reviews/2` from the challenge node (result_uri null, attempt 2). The 404 becomes 'No review is recorded for this run, so no findings are shown on its files' although the review exists and has findings on the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the guarded run a review section with at least one finding that names GUARDED_NOTES_PATH, at a review attempt different from the challenge's attempts. In inert-markdown, or in a findings-on-files variant, assert that the finding is listed on the captured file.

findings.title: No policy check runs a test of Markdown's unchanged default mode
findings.description: ui-task Constraints require Markdown.tsx's default behaviour and every existing caller outside src/projects/ to stay unchanged. The change refactors the default `img` (the new unavailableImage helper) and `table` (an extracted const). The only tests of the default mode (live https links with noopener, remote https images loaded, the unavailable-image labels, raw HTML kept literal) are in tests/document-render.spec.ts, part of the root e2e suite. The policy's ui and controller checks run build, test:unit, test:contracts, server/projects.test.ts, workflow.run_tests and the project-workflows Playwright config, none of which covers it, and no unit test renders Markdown. Reading the code, the default output is equivalent today, but nothing executed confirms it.
findings.failure_scenario: A later edit, or this one, changes the default `img` or `a`, for example sharing inertComponents or dropping `loading="lazy"`/`rel`. Every check the policy runs passes, and the document viewer regresses unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `npx --no-install playwright test tests/document-render.spec.ts` (with the root config) as a ui check in the policy, or add a small unit test that renders <Markdown> with and without `inert` (react-dom/server) and asserts the markup of each mode.

findings.title: The path-leak assertions on the new sections cannot fail: the guarded texts contain no path
findings.description: guardrails.spec.ts calls `renderedText()` on the challenge page (line 130), the completion (157), the questions (208) and the decisions (237) to assert that no /tmp/ or /home/ path leaks. `leak` reaches only the task texts, via rawLaneWorker. GUARDED_DECISIONS, the CHALLENGE_* strings, GUARDED_QUESTIONS, GUARDED_UNTESTED and GUARDED_VERIFY_YOURSELF contain no absolute path. The server redacts these fields (projects.ts projectInputs) and server/projects.test.ts tests that, but the browser assertions are vacuous.
findings.failure_scenario: If server/projects.ts stopped redacting decisions, concerns, questions or verify_yourself, the candidate-phase guardrails tests would still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: In guardedInputsSection, put `leak` into decisions, one concern message, one question and verify_yourself. Redact the same fields in the fixture projection so the worker phase matches.

data.notes: Scope: the coverage brief applied to the ui scenarios of PRD section 6 slice 2, every ui-task Acceptance bullet, and the existing scenarios the task says must keep passing. I read guardrails.spec.ts, fixtures.ts, seed.ts and support.ts, the playwright config, the UI sources (Challenge.tsx, WorkerInputs.tsx, NodeDetail.tsx, Assignment.tsx, CreatedFiles.tsx, status.ts, Markdown.tsx), the server projection, and the run's ui packets and logs. I ran nothing: no tests, no Playwright. What holds up: - Scenario ids: each of the five appears in exactly one test title (guardrails.spec.ts:80, 140, 183, 225, 250). Each attaches `screenshot:` and asserts the section 6 list: challenge first in graph and list, the P1 then P2 grouping (fixture order is reversed, so sorting is really tested), consequences, alternative, experiment, accepted reason, attempts and 'one print job'; evidence fields and the legacy null wording; answered and waiting questions with times; decisions rendered or 'none'; inert captured file and decisions. - Phases: the candidate phase goes through the real server/projects.ts over a seeded raw 1.5.0 export. The seed's inputs shape matches export_state.py (challenge validated against challenge.schema.json with additionalProperties false, then run_id and version stripped and attempts added). - Candidate evidence: 31/31 browser tests passed at 1ab6b95 (candidate/ui/2/check-2.log). The gate was blocked only by the screenshot count that 7c5e37e fixes. The existing scenarios executor-marks, created-file-rendered, output-first-task-collapsed, findings-on-files, findings-by-reviewer, legacy-run and paths-redacted are unchanged and among those 31. inert-markdown: - The test records every request with `page.on('request')`, registered before `goto`. That event fires even though `page.route` then aborts non-local URLs, so a real fetch would be recorded; the worker-phase API mocks only match local URLs and do not interfere. - In inert mode the page never tries to load the remote URLs, because no element carries href, src or srcset. The final `remote == []` check is therefore a backstop. - The real guard is the DOM assertions: no `a`, no `img`, no `[href]/[src]/[srcset]`, the inert link and image placeholders, and raw `` kept literal. They run after `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`, so a regression back to the lazy `` would both fail those assertions and be recorded as a request. - `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` after the SPA tab click returns immediately. That is harmless, because requests are recorded when they start. - Worker tasks are inert on the Assignment tab (`data-inert` is asserted). On the launch-node TaskPanel (WorkerInputs.tsx:60) they are inert but not asserted; the task fixtures carry no remote content. Controller assumptions, as they affect the viewer: - 2.1.0 compatibility: pre-1.5.0 exports (RUN_FILES, RUN_SUCCEEDED) are tested for no challenge node, null evidence, no questions and no decisions. A 1.5.0 export of a 2.1.0 feature is covered only by the server test, which is enough since the payload is identical. Seen outside my area and not verified, for the controller or general reviewer: while a challenge rerun is in progress (challenge.running.json), challenge.json still holds the previous paused attempt. projectSnapshot takes the node status from that record ('paused') ahead of the 'running' event.
